name: COO
their_version: the analysts are slow; nine days must become three

number_they_would_believe: median turnaround days in the pilot branches
engagement: signs the problem statement and the will-not-do list; weekly readout (Day 29); decides sponsor-side conflicts

name: Srinivas, credit-ops team lead, Hyderabad
their_version: files arrive incomplete and my people spend the week chasing branches
they_want: the queue visible, fewer chases, no blame for a wrong field
engagement: floor walk and counts in week 1; reviews the workflow map (Day 6); co-owns enablement

name: Credit-ops team lead, Vijayawada
their_version: the tracker is the real system; the SOP is a story
they_want: the tracker's job done properly by something that will not lose a file
engagement: first user of the review page; owns the tracker migration with the FDE

name: 40 credit-ops analysts (Hyderabad and Vijayawada)
their_version: we wait three days for the branch to resend a document, then the core batch runs overnight
they_want: less re-keying, fewer chases, a tool that does not add a step
number_they_would_believe: analyst hours per file; send-back rate
engagement: 8 to 10 interviewed and shadowed (Day 6); pilot workshop (Day 31); adoption tracked (Day 33)

name: Lakshmi (Vijayawada) and one senior analyst (Hyderabad), eval owners
their_version: a field is correct when I would have typed it; a file is complete when the branch would not get it back
they_want: not to be blamed for the model's mistakes; their judgement written down as the standard
number_they_would_believe: field-level accuracy on the files they labelled
engagement: label 30 files in week 2 and the golden set from week 3 (Day 14); first to see every failure

name: Senior analyst, Hyderabad (the sceptic)
their_version: it will never read handwritten income proofs; the 2019 OCR pilot did not
they_want: to be proved right, or shown the failures honestly
number_they_would_believe: the handwritten files flagged for review instead of guessed
engagement: one hour in week 1 to extract her failure model; invited to the pilot workshop

name: CISO
their_version: where does the PDF go; does your model train on our data; which country is the server in
they_want: no data incident with her name on it; no vendor holding production credentials
number_they_would_believe: passed security review; VPC in AWS Mumbai; nothing leaves India
engagement: questionnaire from week 2 (Day 23); deployment model argued with her in the room (Day 21); monthly thereafter

name: Compliance head
their_version: no customer PII leaves India; no mandatory KYC document is ever skipped
they_want: zero audit findings caused by the tool; the rules in writing
number_they_would_believe: zero completeness misses; accuracy on KYC fields
engagement: a fifteen-minute call in week 1 for her first sentence; the full session in week 2; signs the completeness rules as code (Day 11); a week of her time for the acceptable-alternatives list; stands in for the auditor

name: Core-system owner (IT, the 2009 core lending system)
their_version: three vendors have broken this system before; the 6 pm batch window is not negotiable
they_want: no duplicate records, no surprise load, a sandbox refresh he controls
number_they_would_believe: zero duplicate records; every call inside the batch window
engagement: sandbox spike in week 2 (Day 2's Thursday); named in the integration workstream (Day 16); his conditions in the will-not-do list

name: Corporate IT identity team (Active Directory, SSO)
their_version: raise a ticket and we will look at it in the next sprint; nobody gets a service account without the CISO
they_want: nothing that breaks the nightly HR sync
number_they_would_believe: service account approved; group filtering verified by them
engagement: access ticket in week 2; SSO and group filtering designed with them (Day 22)

name: Branch managers (300; Kukatpally first)
their_version: credit-ops sends files back for no reason and the customer blames us
they_want: fewer send-backs; to be told on day one what is missing
engagement: a call with the Kukatpally manager in week 2; in the pilot from week 7; the resubmission flow designed with him; branch isolation respected (Day 15)

name: RBI auditor
their_version: show me the decision, who made it, and the documents it rested on
they_want: documented, reviewable decisions with a human accountable for each
number_they_would_believe: an audit trail per file with a human decision
engagement: never met; the compliance head speaks for him; the audit trail is in the skeleton from week 3 (Day 20)

name: Kaagaz CEO and engagement lead (our side)
their_version: is this FDE-shaped, and will a second lender buy the same pattern
they_want: recurring revenue and patterns for product (Day 3)
number_they_would_believe: ARR that survives the FDE leaving; the second-customer test
